title: Prepositions & Locative Semi-Prepositions (Ẓurūf)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 47; Ryding Ch. 16)
objectives: Distinguish true prepositions (حُرُوفُ الجَرِّ: فِي, مِنْ, إِلَى, عَلَى, عَنْ, بِـ, لِـ) from locative/temporal nouns (ظُرُوفٌ: قَبْلَ, بَعْدَ, أَمَامَ, خَلْفَ).
Recognize idiomatic verb–preposition pairs whose meaning shifts with the preposition.
Parse prepositional phrases (جَارٌّ وَمَجْرُورٌ) and adverbial ẓurūf + iḍāfah.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 4: Which case do true prepositions govern on the following noun?

sections.heading: True Prepositions vs. Ẓurūf
sections.body: True prepositions (ḥurūf al-jarr) are invariable particles that govern a noun in the genitive case. Semi-prepositions (ẓurūf, such as قَبْلَ 'before', بَعْدَ 'after', عِنْدَ 'at/with', فَوْقَ 'above', تَحْتَ 'under') are actually nouns of time or place in the adverbial accusative acting as muḍāf before a genitive muḍāf ilayh.

sections.label: Idiomatic Verb–Preposition Shifts
sections.summary: Changing the preposition after a verb can completely reverse its meaning: رَغِبَ فِي ('to desire') vs. رَغِبَ عَنْ ('to turn away from / dislike'); دَعَا لِـ ('to pray for') vs. دَعَا عَلَى ('to invoke against').

sections.heading: True Prepositions vs. Ẓurūf
rows: فِي, مِنْ, إِلَى, عَلَى, عَنْ, بِـ, لِـ, كَـ
قَبْلَ, بَعْدَ, عِنْدَ, بَيْنَ, فَوْقَ, تَحْتَ
Ẓarf itself becomes genitive after مِنْ!

sections.translation: The student sat in front of the teacher.
sections.irab: أَمَامَ: ظَرْفُ مَكَانٍ مَنْصُوبٌ وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ | المُعَلِّمِ: مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ مَجْرُورٌ بِالكَسْرَةِ
sections.notes: أَمَامَ takes fatḥah (accusative) as a ẓarf and governs المُعَلِّمِ in the genitive as muḍāf ilayh.

sections.heading: Helping Vowels on مِنْ and عَنْ
sections.body: Before hamzat al-waṣl, مِنْ takes fatḥah (مِنَ البَيْتِ) while عَنْ takes kasrah (عَنِ المَدِينَةِ).
